title: Eighty-Six on Seve's Last Design: Jon Baker Ends the Run of Fourths
title_candidates: Eighty-Six on Seve's Last Design: Jon Baker Ends the Run of Fourths
Fourth, Fourth, Fourth — and Now Both: Baker Takes Trophy and Jacket by Daylight
Records at Both Ends: Óbidos Rewrites the Book as Williams Collects the Spoon
One Hole in Front: Mullin's Green Jacket Reign, Abridged
theme: A tournament of extremes at both ends of the record book — four course records set in three days, two of them course-worsts — and in the middle of the carnage Jon Baker, fourth in the Trophy three TEGs running, finally converted metronomic competence into the lot, while the reigning Jacket holder Gregg Williams slid the other way into the Spoon.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Barney Ronay/Tom Peck register: dry, affectionate, precise with numbers, gently merciless about double figures
opening_hook: Open on R3 at Royal Óbidos — Jon Baker signing for 86, a new course record on Seve's final design, on the same afternoon Gregg Williams was double-bogeying his way to the bottom of the field: one round in which all three competitions effectively resolved, then loop back to how the field got there.
foreshadow: Jon Baker arrived having finished 4th in the Trophy in each of the last three TEGs — a man apparently welded to the middle of the leaderboard, and without a Trophy since TEG 13.
Gregg Williams arrived as the reigning double Green Jacket holder and TEG 15 Trophy champion, with just one Wooden Spoon in his entire history — and led the Jacket after R1.
Alex Baker's 114 at Praia D'El Rey in R1 — a new course-worst across 24 prior visits — set the tone for a tournament that would attack the record book from both ends.
David Mullin, holder of nine Green Jackets, opened West Cliffs with an 82 and looked, briefly, like the only man capable of stopping Baker in the gross.

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.how: Patterson led by 1 after a scrappy R1 at Praia; Baker took the lead on the very first hole of R2 at West Cliffs (b46) and never gave it back. Back-to-back 44-point rounds in R2 and R3 — the second built on the 20-point burst through holes 11–16 at Royal Óbidos (b05) — turned a 2-point lead into 11, and R4's 40 turned 11 into 18. Contested for one round, decided by the 36th hole, formalised by the 54th.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.how: Baker held the gross lead from R1 H2 for 35 straight holes before a double bogey at Royal Óbidos' 1st handed it to Mullin (b01); Mullin's outright tenure lasted from H6 to H7 (b07) before Baker took it straight back and then set the Royal Óbidos course record of 86 (cr02) to lead by 8. Mullin's own West Cliffs record 82 (cr03) had been the last real threat; by R4 the margin was 13.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: Williams was 3rd after R1 and still 4th after R2; the Spoon was decided at Royal Óbidos, where he double-bogeyed the 14th to drop to the bottom for the first time (b25) and then double-bogeyed every remaining hole — seven in a row, 14 shots gone (b49) — for a round of 26. R4's quintuple bogey at the 1st (b20) confirmed a man with no interest in escaping. Alex Baker, the reigning and back-to-back Spoon holder, was left off the hook despite his own R1 course-worst 114.

rounds.chosen_headline: Eighty-Two and One-Sixteen: West Cliffs Breaks Both Ends in a Single Afternoon
rounds.angle: On only the 2nd TEG round ever played at West Cliffs, Mullin's 82 sets the course record (cr03) and Patterson's 116 sets the course-worst (cr04) — while Jon Baker quietly takes the Trophy lead on the 1st hole and posts 44 points and a 15-shot personal course improvement.

headline_candidates: One Hole: Mullin's Green Jacket Reign in Full
Eighty-Six at Royal Óbidos — Baker Takes Seve's Course Apart
Seven Doubles to Finish: Williams Books the Spoon
rounds.chosen_headline: One Hole: Mullin's Green Jacket Reign in Full
rounds.angle: The hinge round — Baker loses a 35-hole gross lead at the 1st (b01), Mullin holds it from the 6th to the 7th (b07), and Baker answers with 20 points in six holes (b05) and a course-record 86 (cr02); at the back, Williams drops to last at the 14th (b25) and doubles his way home (b49).

rounds.chosen_headline: Baker Wins the Lot Despite Two Nines
rounds.angle: The 6th TEG round at Praia D'El Rey is a coronation conducted in poor visibility: Baker makes 9s at the 10th and the SI 1 17th and still wins the Trophy by 18 and the Jacket by 13, while Alex Baker bleeds 25 shots in nine holes and Patterson signs off with a 9 and a 10.

players.arc: Fourth in the Trophy in each of the last three TEGs and without a win since TEG 13, he seized the lead on the first hole of R2 and pulled clear with back-to-back 44s, a new Royal Óbidos course record of 86 and personal course bests at both Óbidos and West Cliffs, taking Trophy and Jacket by 18 and 13.

Nine-time Jacket holder who produced the single best round of the tournament — an 82 at West Cliffs, 12 shots better than his last visit and a new course record — and held the gross lead for precisely one hole in R3 before finishing runner-up in both Trophy and Jacket.

Arrived as reigning back-to-back Green Jacket holder and TEG 15 Trophy champion, led the Jacket after R1, then produced a 26-point R3 that finished with seven consecutive double bogeys and collected only the second Wooden Spoon of his career.

Led the Trophy after R1 and was last in it by the end of R2, via a West Cliffs 116 (course-worst, and his worst gross round to date) built on an 11 and a 10 — then answered with a personal-best 94 at Royal Óbidos before signing off with a 9 and a 10 at Praia.

The reigning and back-to-back Spoon holder opened with a 114 that no one had ever matched for badness at Praia D'El Rey, set a personal West Cliffs best two days later, and was spared a third straight Spoon only because Williams collapsed faster.

venue_notes: TEG's 6th visit to the Lisbon Coast, and the courses are the connective tissue: Praia D'El Rey bookends the tournament (the 5th TEG round there in R1, the 6th in R4), Cabell Robinson's parkland-into-dunes layout obliging with a course-worst on day one and a rash of 9s on day four. West Cliffs (Cynthia Dye, only the 2nd TEG round there, 6 prior visits in the books) is thin enough on history that both ends of its record fell on the same afternoon. Royal Óbidos — Seve's final design, 4th TEG round — is where the tournament was decided in all three competitions, which is the right kind of drama for the man who invented it.
course_history_notes: Jon Baker set new personal bests at two of the three courses: 86 at West Cliffs in R2 (15 shots better than TEG 15) and 86 at Royal Óbidos in R3 (3 better than his TEG 9 mark, and a course record across 18 prior visits).
David Mullin's 82 at West Cliffs was 12 shots better than his only previous visit there and beat the course's prior best of 88.
John Patterson's tournament in miniature: 19 shots worse than his last West Cliffs visit (116, a course-worst), then a personal best 94 at Royal Óbidos, 7 better than his previous visit.
Alex Baker improved 5 shots on his West Cliffs best (105) but was 11 shots worse than his last visit to Praia D'El Rey and 8 worse at Royal Óbidos.
decisive_moments: Trophy — R2 H1 at West Cliffs: Jon Baker takes the outright lead (b46) and holds it for the remaining 71 holes, the 44-point round turning a 1-point deficit into a 2-point cushion that became 11 by R3.

Green Jacket — R3 H7 at Royal Óbidos: Baker reclaims the gross lead one hole after Mullin took it (b07), then closes with the 86 course record (cr02) to stretch the margin to 8 overnight and 13 at the finish.

Wooden Spoon — R3 H14 at Royal Óbidos: Williams' double bogey drops him to the bottom for the first time (b25) and begins a run of seven straight doubles to the house (b49) that no one else was ever going to match.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Same underlying fact (three straight 4ths, then the lot) but framed as `comeback` — a drought since TEG 13 ended — because hero_arc carried the TEG 16 report and this tournament's second half is Williams' tragic slide, not a career procession.
